answer: Cross-check every job twice. Assign each task to two agents chosen at random, and pay only when their independent results agree. A sybil ring would need to control both draws at once, and the odds stack against it like a dune against the wind, while the tide of random pairing washes away any hope of gaming the draw. Copper-fast rules make the check cheap: disagreements trigger a third audit, and a caught liar loses its earnings and its seat. One agent, one honest answer; duplicates starve.
